name: unrehearsed-2026-10-10-third
_note: DD-0 S3 third blind author set, written blind on Oct 10, 2026 by an author who never saw the corpus, the tests, the docs or the two earlier blind files; 300 orders, each with its intended reading; never edited after the run.

intended.note: Ney should attack the only visible enemy adjacent to him (Mack at Swabia) or be asked which enemy; a misread is any other marshal acting or a move instead of an attack.

orders.line: Right then, I think it's time Marshal Ney went and gave Mack a bloody nose at Swabia

intended.note: Ney attacks Mack at Swabia; a misread is treating the chatty framing as a move to Swabia or picking up 'nose' or 'bloody' as something else.

orders.line: Marshal Davout will engage General Mack's army at Swabia forthwith

intended.note: Davout attacks Mack; a misread is a march to Swabia without battle, or a hold.
Typo 'atack' must still be read as attack by Davout on Mack; a misread is an unknown-command reply.
A politely phrased question is an order; Soult must attack Mack rather than the game answering a question about whether he could.

orders.line: Murat, charge Mack, the cavalry is fresh

intended.note: Murat makes a cavalry charge on Mack; the reason tail must not become a drill or recruit of cavalry.
Name after the verb: Ney is the attacker, Mack the target; a misread swaps them or asks who should attack.

orders.line: Massena, hit Archduke John in the Tyrol

intended.note: Massena attacks John at Tyrol; a misread is a march to Tyrol, or attacking Mack.

orders.line: Bernadotte strikes Archduke John at Tyrol at once

intended.note: Bernadotte attacks John; 'at once' is urgency, not a target; a misread is a move or a hold.

orders.line: The Iron Marshal is to fall upon Mack immediately

intended.note: The Iron Marshal is Davout; a misread is asking which marshal or picking Ney.

orders.line: the bravest of the brave attacks the austrians in swabia

intended.note: The epithet is Ney; 'the austrians in swabia' is Mack; a misread is attacking Austria as a nation (diplomacy) or asking for a marshal.
Lannes attacks Mack from Franche-Comte (Swabia is adjacent); a misread is a plain move to Swabia with no battle.

orders.line: Soult, engage the enemy at Swabia and don't stop until they're broken

intended.note: Soult attacks Mack; the tail about not stopping may be read as a pursue follow-on but must not replace the attack.

orders.line: Ney attack Mack and Davout support him

intended.note: Compound: Ney attacks Mack AND Davout supports Ney; the second half, Davout's support, must not be dropped silently.

orders.line: I want Davout to attack Mack while Ney holds the Rhineland

intended.note: Davout attacks Mack and Ney holds Rhineland; a misread is Ney attacking, or the hold being lost.

orders.line: Prince Murat will charge the Austrian cavalry at Swabia

intended.note: Prince Murat is Murat; he charges Mack at Swabia; a misread is recruiting cavalry or asking who Prince Murat is.
Attacking the province Tyrol means attacking the enemy holding it (John); a misread is a plain march to Tyrol or an unknown target.
The Guard is Napoleon's own command at Lorraine; it attacks Mack at Swabia; a misread is asking which marshal 'the Guard' is.

orders.line: The Emperor himself will lead the assault on Swabia

intended.note: The Emperor is Napoleon; he attacks Mack at Swabia; a misread is any other marshal or a move.
Telegraphic list: Ney attacks Mack at Swabia; a misread is a move or asking which of the three names is the target.

orders.line: Davout — assault Mack's position with everything you've got

intended.note: Davout attacks Mack; 'everything you've got' is emphasis not a recruit; the em dash must not break the parse.

orders.line: Marshal Ney is to attack General Mack with all speed; Davout and Soult are to follow in support

intended.note: Ney attacks Mack; Davout and Soult each support Ney; dropping either support silently is a misread.

orders.line: Attack the Austrians at Tyrol, Massena, before John can pull back

intended.note: Massena attacks John at Tyrol; the 'before John can pull back' clause is a reason, not a condition to wait on.
Slang 'go kill' means attack; a misread is a move or an unknown command.

orders.line: Soult, strike Mack from the Lorraine side while Davout comes at him from the Rhineland

intended.note: Soult attacks Mack and Davout attacks or supports against Mack too; 'him' is Mack; losing Davout's half is a misread.
John at Tyrol is not adjacent to Lannes at Franche-Comte; the game should refuse with the reason or plan a march-then-attack; attacking Mack instead is a misread.
Davout attacks Mack; 'please' and 'have' must not derail it.

orders.line: It's Mack's turn. Ney, at him.

intended.note: Ney attacks Mack ('at him'); a misread is an end turn triggered by the word 'turn'.

orders.line: Bernadotte will attack the Tyrol with the whole corps.

intended.note: Bernadotte attacks John in Tyrol; a misread is a move to Tyrol with no battle.
'him' has no antecedent in the line; the game should ask who, or default to the one visible enemy adjacent to Davout (Mack); attacking an ally or own marshal is a misread.
A cavalry charge with no named target: ask which enemy, or charge the adjacent visible enemy Mack; a drill or a move is a misread.

orders.line: Soult, I need you to attack Swabia this turn, no excuses

intended.note: Soult attacks Mack at Swabia; a misread is a move or an end turn.

orders.line: Marshal Massena, you are to engage Archduke John's corps in the Tyrol and drive it back on Vienna

intended.note: Massena attacks John; Vienna is where the enemy should be driven, not Massena's destination; a march to Vienna is a misread.

orders.line: Napoleon attacks Mack with the Guard

intended.note: Napoleon's own command attacks Mack; a misread is asking who 'the Guard' is or picking another marshal.

orders.line: attack mack with ney and davout both

intended.note: Both Ney and Davout attack Mack (a coordinated attack); a misread is only one of them attacking with no mention of the other.
The Austrians adjacent to Ney means Mack at Swabia; a misread is declaring war or a diplomatic act toward Austria.

orders.line: Murat, run down Mack's guns with the cavalry

intended.note: Murat charges Mack; a misread is a pursue (Mack has not retreated) or a recruit of cavalry.

orders.line: Go on Davout, into Swabia, drive Mack out

intended.note: Davout attacks Mack at Swabia; a plain move into Swabia with no battle is a weaker reading but acceptable if the game warns; a hold is a misread.

orders.line: Massena, assault John now, and Bernadotte should hit him from Franconia at the same time

intended.note: Massena attacks John and Bernadotte also attacks or supports against John; dropping Bernadotte is a misread.

orders.line: Ney will attack Mack if Davout can support him

intended.note: Ney attacks Mack with Davout in support (the condition is a request for support, not a reason to do nothing); a misread is nothing happening.
Ney attacks Mack; 'pls' and bare word order must not defeat it.

orders.line: I'd like Ney to attack Mack this turn.

intended.note: Ney attacks Mack; a misread is an end turn or a question answered.

orders.line: Soult to attack the enemy at Swabia with the full corps.

intended.note: Soult attacks Mack; 'the enemy at Swabia' resolves to Mack.

orders.line: Marshal Lannes, advance on Swabia and attack Mack.

intended.note: Lannes attacks Mack at Swabia (adjacent); a misread is a move only, with the attack lost.
A standing pursue order on Mack; a misread is a one-off attack or a move to Swabia.

orders.line: Davout, chase Mack down wherever he runs

intended.note: Pursue Mack; a misread is a simple attack or a scout.

orders.line: Murat, run him down — do not let Mack escape

intended.note: 'him' is Mack (named later in the line); pursue; a misread is asking who 'him' is.
Pursue John; a misread is scouting Tyrol.

orders.line: Pursue the Austrians, Soult, don't let them regroup

intended.note: Soult pursues the adjacent Austrian commander Mack; a misread is a diplomatic act toward Austria.

orders.line: the bravest of the brave is to follow Mack to the ends of the earth

intended.note: Ney pursues Mack; 'the ends of the earth' is not a province; a misread is an unknown destination.

orders.line: Prince Murat, keep on John's heels

intended.note: Murat pursues John; a misread is a hold or asking what 'heels' means.
Bernadotte pursues Mack; a misread is an attack on John instead.
Davout supports Ney; a misread is Davout attacking Ney or Ney moving.
Soult supports Ney; 'back up' is not a retreat.
Lannes supports Murat; a misread is a move with no support relation.

orders.line: Davout will cover the Marshal Ney's advance

intended.note: 'cover' is support; a misread is Davout holding or defending.

orders.line: Bernadotte, support Massena in the Tyrol

intended.note: Bernadotte supports Massena; a misread is Bernadotte attacking Tyrol alone or moving to Tyrol as a plain march.

orders.line: Soult should march to support the Emperor

intended.note: The Emperor is Napoleon; Soult supports him; a misread is a move to Paris or asking who the Emperor is.
Typo 'suport' is support; a misread is an unknown command.

orders.line: Marshal Soult, you will second Ney's attack and reinforce him should he engage

intended.note: Soult supports Ney; 'second' here is not a number or an order of time; a misread is Soult attacking.

orders.line: stand behind Ney, Davout, in case Mack turns on him

intended.note: Davout supports Ney; a misread is Davout attacking Mack directly or holding.
Murat supports Lannes; a misread is a charge on Lannes or a move to Franche-Comte with no support.
Napoleon supports Soult; a misread is asking who the Guard is.

orders.line: Davout: support Ney. Soult: support Davout.

intended.note: Two supports: Davout to Ney and Soult to Davout; silently dropping Soult's half is a misread.

orders.line: Massena, attack John; if he retreats, pursue him into Vienna

intended.note: Massena attacks John now; the conditional pursue is a follow-on; a misread is only pursuing, or a march to Vienna.

orders.line: if Mack moves, Ney attacks him

intended.note: A conditional attack on Mack by Ney (either as a conditional order or an attack with the game explaining it cannot wait); a misread is Ney moving.
Ney attacks Mack at Swabia; a misread is a move to Swabia.
Davout attacks Mack (the only sensible reading of a marshal, an enemy and 'go'); a misread is a move toward Mack's location with no battle, or an unknown command.

orders.line: Ney, fall on Mack's flank; Murat, charge his centre

intended.note: Ney attacks Mack and Murat charges Mack ('his' is Mack); dropping Murat's half is a misread.
Soult attacks Mack at Swabia; 'at dawn' is flavour, not a delay.

orders.line: Massena is to attack the Archduke immediately and with all speed

intended.note: 'the Archduke' adjacent to Massena is John (Charles is not in sight); a misread is asking which Archduke when only one is visible, or a move.

orders.line: Ney and Davout, attack Mack together

intended.note: A joint attack by Ney and Davout on Mack; a misread is only one of them acting with no word about the other.
Murat charges the adjacent Austrian commander Mack; a misread is a diplomatic act toward Austria.
Typo 'mvoe' is move; Davout marches to Frankfurt; a misread is an unknown command or a move elsewhere.

orders.line: could Lannes please march to Munich

intended.note: The march must go to Munich, not back to Lorraine, and the question form is an order.
Ney moves to Frankfurt; a misread is an attack on anyone there.
Soult moves to Brabant; a misread is a different province or a hold.

orders.line: Marshal Bernadotte will proceed to Dresden forthwith

intended.note: Bernadotte moves to Dresden (Saxony is at peace; the game may warn about entering neutral land but the destination must be Dresden).

orders.line: Massena, take the army to Piedmont

intended.note: Massena moves to Piedmont; a misread is a retreat or a scout.
Murat moves to Bern; a misread is Lannes moving or a scout.

orders.line: Ney to Nassau, with all speed

intended.note: Ney moves to Nassau; 'with all speed' is urgency not a target.

orders.line: Napoleon moves the Guard to Rhineland

intended.note: Napoleon moves to Rhineland; a misread is a different marshal or a support of Ney/Davout.
Napoleon marches to Paris (several steps away, so a multi-turn march order is fine); a misread is asking who the Emperor is or refusing because Paris is not adjacent.
Soult moves to Orleanais; a misread is a diplomatic 'send' (mission).

orders.line: I want Lannes in Munich by next turn

intended.note: Lannes moves to Munich; 'by next turn' is not an end turn.

orders.line: Davout, go to Gelderland and wait there

intended.note: Davout moves to Gelderland (and then holds); a misread is a hold at Rhineland with no move.
Bernadotte moves to Munich; a misread is a scout.
Massena moves to Munich; a misread is an attack on John.
A bare destination after a marshal's name is a march to Brabant; a misread is an unknown command.

orders.line: Soult, head for Franche-Comte and join Lannes

intended.note: Soult moves to Franche-Comte (support of Lannes is also an acceptable reading); a misread is Lannes moving to Lorraine.
A march on Swabia, which Mack holds; the game may warn or convert it to an attack, either is fine; a misread is Murat going anywhere else or holding.

orders.line: Davout, bring the corps back to Lorraine

intended.note: Davout moves to Lorraine (a retreat reading is acceptable); a misread is a move to Rhineland or a hold.
Two bare words: Ney marches to Frankfurt; a misread is an unknown command or an attack.

orders.line: Please move Marshal Lannes to Bern.

intended.note: Lannes moves to Bern; a misread is Murat moving.

orders.line: Bernadotte, go to Berlin — no wait, Dresden

intended.note: The self-correction means Dresden, not Berlin; a misread is a march on Berlin (Prussia, at peace) or asking which.

orders.line: Massena advances on Munich with the whole army

intended.note: Massena moves to Munich; a misread is an attack on John at Tyrol.

orders.line: Move Davout and Ney both to Frankfurt

intended.note: Both Davout and Ney move to Frankfurt; moving only one with no word about the other is a misread.

orders.line: Soult, Napoleon, march on Rhineland together

intended.note: Both Soult and Napoleon move to Rhineland; dropping one is a misread.

orders.line: Marshal Soult will relocate his corps to Nivernais.

intended.note: Soult moves to Nivernais; a misread is a retreat flagged as a rout or an unknown destination.

orders.line: Lannes: Swabia, via the shortest road

intended.note: A march on Swabia (enemy-held; a warning or attack conversion is acceptable); a misread is a march elsewhere.
Ney holds in place; a misread is a move or a fortify.
Davout holds where he stands; a misread is an unknown command.
Soult holds at Lorraine; a misread is a move.

orders.line: Massena, hold Milan at all costs

intended.note: Massena holds Milan (a defend reading is acceptable); a misread is an attack or a move.
Lannes holds; a misread is a fortify or a move.
Bernadotte holds; the negation 'don't move' must not become a move; an end turn is a misread.
Napoleon holds; a misread is asking who the Guard is.

orders.line: Hold position, Murat — I mean it, no charging

intended.note: Murat holds; the words 'charging' must not become a charge.
Ney holds; a misread is an unknown command.
Soult takes a defensive posture at Lorraine; a misread is an attack or a build of a fort.
Davout defends; a misread is a fortify (acceptable but weaker) or a move.

orders.line: Massena is to defend Milan against anything John sends

intended.note: Massena defends Milan; John's name must not turn this into an attack on John.

orders.line: Ney, take up a defensive position

intended.note: Ney defends where he stands; a misread is a move to some 'position'.
Bernadotte defends Franconia; a misread is an unknown province.

orders.line: Lannes — defend. The Austrians are close.

intended.note: Lannes defends in place; the aside about Austrians must not become an attack on Mack.

orders.line: Marshal Soult will assume a defensive stance until further notice

intended.note: Soult defends; a misread is a hold with no stance change (acceptable) or a fortify of a fort.
Ney retreats to a safe adjacent French province or is asked where; a misread is an attack or a hold.
Massena retreats to Piedmont (a move there is acceptable); a misread is a move to Tyrol.
Bernadotte retreats or moves to Frankfurt; a misread is a different province.
Davout retreats or moves to Lorraine; a misread is unfortify or a hold.
Lannes retreats to Lorraine; a misread is a move for Soult.

orders.line: Soult, pull back — we're not ready

intended.note: Soult retreats (destination may be asked); the reason tail must not become a drill.

orders.line: Murat, get the cavalry out of there, back to Lorraine

intended.note: Murat retreats or moves to Lorraine; a misread is a recruit of cavalry or a charge.
Ney scouts Swabia; a misread is an attack on Mack or a move into Swabia.
Murat scouts Munich; a misread is a move or a diplomatic mission.

orders.line: Bernadotte, have a look at Bohemia

intended.note: 'have a look at' is a scout; a misread is a move into Bohemia.

orders.line: what's in Tyrol? Massena, find out

intended.note: A scout of Tyrol by Massena; a misread is answering the question from the map without ordering anything, or an attack on John.
British spelling 'reconnoitre' is a scout; a misread is an unknown command.
Typo 'scuot' is scout; a misread is a move or an unknown command.

orders.line: Murat, send riders towards Bern and report back

intended.note: A scout of Bern; a misread is a move to Bern or a diplomatic mission to Switzerland.

orders.line: Ney, I need eyes on Nassau

intended.note: A scout of Nassau; a misread is a move or an attack.
'recon' is a scout; a misread is a move to Munich.

orders.line: Soult, dig in — the Austrians are close

intended.note: Soult fortifies at Lorraine; the aside about Austrians must not become an attack.

orders.line: Marshal Soult will fortify his position at Lorraine forthwith

intended.note: Soult fortifies; a misread is building a fort (a construction) or a move.
Ney fortifies; a misread is an unknown command.
'entrench' is fortify; a misread is a hold with nothing dug, or a build.

orders.line: Massena, throw up earthworks around Milan

intended.note: 'earthworks' is fortify; a misread is a build of a fort or a repair.

orders.line: Bernadotte, dig in at Franconia, please

intended.note: Bernadotte fortifies; a misread is a move to Franconia (he is already there).
Lannes fortifies; a misread is a build of a fort or a garrison.
Napoleon fortifies; a misread is asking who the Guard is.

orders.line: Soult, stop digging and get ready to move

intended.note: Soult unfortifies; the phrase 'get ready to move' must not become a move to nowhere; a fortify is the opposite and a misread.
Ney unfortifies; a misread is a retreat or a fortify.
Davout unfortifies; a misread is a fortify.
Davout drills; a misread is a recruit.

orders.line: Ney, put the corps through its paces this turn

intended.note: 'through its paces' is a drill; a misread is a move or an end turn.
Training is a drill; a misread is building a training ground.
Soult drills; a misread is an unknown command.

orders.line: Bernadotte, exercise the troops, they're green

intended.note: Bernadotte drills; 'green' is a reason, not a colour or a recruit.

orders.line: Lannes, have the men practise their musketry

intended.note: Lannes drills; a misread is a recruit of infantry or an attack.
Ney forms square; a misread is a fortify or a hold.
Soult forms square; the mention of cavalry must not become a recruit of cavalry or an attack.
Massena forms square; a misread is a move to a province named Square.

orders.line: Davout, leave 3,000 men to garrison Rhineland

intended.note: Davout detaches a 3,000-man garrison in Rhineland; a misread is a recruit of 3,000 or a hold.

orders.line: Soult, detach a garrison for Lorraine

intended.note: Soult garrisons Lorraine (the size may be asked); a misread is a fortify.
Massena garrisons Milan with 5,000; a misread is a recruit of 5,000 in Milan.
Ney garrisons Rhineland; a misread is a hold.

orders.line: Leave a garrison in Franche-Comte, Lannes, two thousand will do

intended.note: Lannes garrisons Franche-Comte with 2,000 (the words, not digits); a misread is Murat acting or a recruit.

orders.line: Bernadotte, drop off a few battalions to hold Franconia

intended.note: A garrison of Franconia (size may be asked); a misread is a plain hold with no detachment.
Raise infantry in Paris; a recruit must raise infantry, not cavalry, and in Paris.
Recruit 5,000 cavalry in Lorraine; a misread is infantry, or a different province.

orders.line: I need more guns — recruit artillery in Rhineland

intended.note: Recruit artillery in Rhineland; a misread is infantry or a build.
Recruit in Lyonnais with the type unspecified (default to infantry or ask); a misread is refusing because no type was given.

orders.line: Raise a new regiment of foot at Champagne.

intended.note: 'foot' is infantry; recruit infantry in Champagne; a misread is cavalry or an unknown unit type.
'horsemen' is cavalry; recruit cavalry in Burgundy; a misread is infantry.
Recruit 10,000 infantry in Ile-de-France; a misread is enacting a conscription law.
A recruit of infantry in Lorraine; naming Soult must not derail it into a drill or a refusal.

orders.line: more cannon, Normandy, as many as 800 gold buys

intended.note: Recruit artillery in Normandy up to the treasury; a misread is infantry, or a build.
Build a depot in Lorraine; a misread is a fort or a different province.
Build a fort (construction) in Rhineland; a misread is a marshal fortifying.

orders.line: Put up a market in Paris

intended.note: Build a market in Paris; a misread is a depot or an unknown command.
Build stables in Burgundy; a misread is a recruit of cavalry.

orders.line: Construct a training ground at Franche-Comte

intended.note: Build a training ground; a misread is a drill by Lannes or Murat.

orders.line: Davout, build a depot in Rhineland

intended.note: Build a depot in Rhineland; Davout's name must not cause a refusal or a fortify.
Build a fort in Lorraine; a misread is Soult or Napoleon fortifying.

orders.line: I want a supply depot in Savoy

intended.note: Build a depot in Savoy; a misread is a different building or province.
Build a market in Flanders; a misread is an unknown command.
Repair Lorraine; a misread is a build or a fortify.
Repair Rhineland; a misread is a fortify by Ney or Davout.

orders.line: Have the engineers fix up Franche-Comte

intended.note: 'fix up' is repair; a misread is a build or a fortify.
Propose an alliance to Prussia; a misread is a non-aggression pact or a declaration of war.
A peace proposal to Austria without naming Talleyrand; a misread is an alliance or asking who should carry it.
Ask Britain for peace terms; a misread is offering tribute or declaring war.
Propose non-aggression (or peace first, since we are at war) to Russia; a misread is an alliance.
A diplomatic mission to Denmark; a misread is moving a marshal to Copenhagen.

orders.line: Talleyrand, see if the Prussians will sign a non-aggression pact

intended.note: Propose non-aggression to Prussia; a misread is an alliance.

orders.line: Let's make peace with Russia, Talleyrand, whatever it costs

intended.note: A peace proposal to Russia; the 'whatever it costs' tail may add generous terms but must not become tribute alone.
Propose an alliance to Sweden; a misread is a mission or non-aggression.
Three bare words: propose an alliance to Prussia; a misread is an unknown command.

orders.line: Ask the Austrians what they want for peace

orders.line: I want an alliance with the Ottomans against Russia

orders.line: Talleyrand, propose a non-aggression treaty with Saxony

orders.line: offer tribute to Britain for peace

orders.line: Talleyrand, send an envoy to Naples

orders.line: Could we try for peace with Austria? Talleyrand, make them an offer.

intended.note: A peace proposal to Austria; a misread is answering the question without acting.
Alliance proposal to Hesse; a misread is non-aggression or an unknown nation.

orders.line: Peace with Britain. Now. Whatever Pitt wants.

Propose or impose vassalage on Naples; a misread is an alliance or a declaration of war.

orders.line: Talleyrand, I want Saxony as a satellite

Make Hanover a vassal; a misread is a move to Hanover or a declaration of war.

orders.line: Put some gold into the Kingdom of Italy

Invest 100 gold in Switzerland; a misread is a diplomatic proposal.
Cede the province Flanders to the vassal Holland; a misread is investing in Holland or a move.

orders.line: Cede Savoy to the Kingdom of Italy

orders.line: Talleyrand, we are at war with Naples as of today

Declare war on Sweden; a misread is a proposal.

orders.line: War with Portugal. Inform their ambassador.

Break the Spanish alliance; a misread is a declaration of war on Spain or a refusal because Spain is an ally.

A peace or ceasefire proposal to Russia; a misread is an alliance.

orders.line: Offer the Papal States a non-aggression pact

A peace proposal to Austria; the abbreviation 'w' must not break it.
A diplomatic mission to Prussia (Berlin is the court); a misread is moving a marshal to Berlin.

orders.line: Propose an alliance with Denmark against Britain

orders.line: Offer Austria peace: they keep Vienna, we keep everything else

Non-aggression proposal to Sardinia; a misread is an unknown nation.
